title: The Damaged Life: Frankfurt, Vienna, Oxford, California, and the Return
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Frankfurt, Schöne Aussicht 9
stops.date_confidence: attested. Birth date and city confirmed by en.wikipedia and de.wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno'. The street address Schöne Aussicht 9 is carried by the geographic dossier and its coordinate falls on the riverside street it names; the house number itself was not re-verified against a cadastral source.
stops.campa: Theodor Ludwig Wiesengrund is born in an apartment on the Schöne Aussicht, the embankment street that looks across the Main. His father Oscar is a wine merchant, Jewish by descent and Protestant by conversion; his mother Maria Calvelli-Adorno della Piana is a singer of Corsican and Italian descent, Catholic, who has performed under her own name. He is their only child. He will sign himself with his mother's name and keep his father's abbreviated to a W. Her sister Agathe, a pianist, lives in the house.
suggested_refs: The Schöne Aussicht embankment, Frankfurt am Main, before the 1944 bombing

stops.name: Amorbach, the summers in the Odenwald
stops.date_confidence: traditional. de.wikipedia, 'Theodor W. Adorno', records Amorbach as the family's recurring summer place and as a subject of Adorno's own later essays. No individual summer is dated in any source consulted, and no house was located; 1910 is an ordering date inside the attested span of the childhood summers.
stops.campa: Each summer the family leaves the city for this small town in the Odenwald, under the sandstone abbey and the wooded hills. The boy walks the same paths year after year and learns the names of the villages around. He writes about Amorbach as a grown man, in a short essay that treats the place as evidence: a kind of life existed here, and what replaced it can be measured against it. No summer of his is dated in the record, and no house in the town has been identified as the one the family took.
suggested_refs: Adorno's essay 'Amorbach', collected in Ohne Leitbild

stops.name: Sachsenhausen, the gymnasium on the Hedderichstraße
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the span 1913-1921 and the 1921 Abitur (en.wikipedia). The school's name is a trap: per de.wikipedia, 'Freiherr-vom-Stein-Schule (Frankfurt am Main)', it was renamed Kaiser Wilhelms-Gymnasium only in 1917 and Freiherr-vom-Stein-Schule in 1945, so the name usually attached to Adorno is anachronistic for his entry year. The coordinate is placed on the historic Hedderichstraße building (inaugurated 1911, demolished in the 1960s or 1970s) rather than on the 2007-2009 Schweizer Straße campus that geocoders return.
stops.campa: He enters the Frankfurt gymnasium in Sachsenhausen at ten and leaves it at seventeen with the Abitur, first in his class. On Saturday afternoons he reads the Critique of Pure Reason with Siegfried Kracauer, fourteen years his senior, who takes Kant not as a system to be mastered but as a coded document to be read for its wounds and its silences. Adorno will say afterward that he owes those Saturdays more than he owes any academic teacher. Alongside school he takes private composition lessons with Bernhard Sekles.
suggested_refs: The Hedderichstraße school building, Frankfurt-Sachsenhausen, 1911-1960s

stops.name: Frankfurt-Oberrad, Seeheimer Straße 19
stops.date_confidence: attested as the family address from 1914 (de.wikipedia). The Stolperstein at the door is recorded by de.wikipedia without an installation year; the year is a gap and the mention is reconstruction as to date only.
stops.campa: The household moves out to Oberrad, a village swallowed by the city on its southeastern edge, and this becomes the family address for the rest of his German youth. Four-hand piano transcriptions of the Viennese classics fill the evenings, played with his aunt Agathe; his mother's singers and accompanists pass through the rooms. He learns the symphonic repertoire from the inside, at a keyboard, years before he hears most of it in a hall. A brass Stolperstein is set into the pavement outside this door long afterward.
suggested_refs: The Stolperstein at Seeheimer Straße 19, Frankfurt-Oberrad

segments.name: Frankfurt, Vienna, and the Circle Around Schoenberg

stops.name: University of Frankfurt, the Jügelhaus
stops.date_confidence: attested. Matriculation 1921 and the 1924 doctorate on Husserl under Hans Cornelius are given by both en.wikipedia and the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy. The month of matriculation is an ordering convention.
stops.campa: He matriculates at eighteen in philosophy, psychology, sociology and music, and finds in Hans Cornelius a neo-Kantian who teaches without a system and lets a student argue back. In three years he writes a doctorate on the phenomenology of Husserl and takes the degree at twenty-one, in a university that will not keep him. Music remains the other half of every day: composition lessons, the piano, the scores of the Viennese classics he has played four-hand since childhood. In February 1925 he goes to Vienna to study composition.
suggested_refs: The Jügelhaus, Frankfurt's university building on the Bockenheimer Landstraße
sources: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

stops.name: Frankfurt, the year Benjamin appears
stops.date_confidence: contested, and the contradiction is left standing. en.wikipedia, 'Walter Benjamin', places the acquaintance in 1923 in the Frankfurt context, where Benjamin was pursuing his habilitation and where the Institute for Social Research was founded that year. The geographic dossier had placed the meeting in Berlin through a circle around Ernst Bloch; neither the Berlin location nor the Bloch attribution could be confirmed in any source consulted. de.wikipedia dates the deepening of the friendship instead to a stay with Kracauer on the Gulf of Naples in September 1925. Month arbitrary.
stops.campa: In the year the Institute for Social Research is founded in this city, a private scholar named Walter Benjamin is in Frankfurt trying to habilitate, and the two become acquainted. Benjamin is eleven years older and already writing in a manner that has no discipline willing to hold it. Adorno takes from him a way of reading fragments as though they were arguments, and the correspondence that follows runs seventeen years. When and where the two actually met is unsettled: one account puts it here in 1923, another dates the friendship's deepening to a stay with Kracauer on the Gulf of Naples in September 1925.
suggested_refs: The Adorno-Benjamin correspondence, 1928-1940
sources: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

stops.name: Berlin, Gretel Karplus
stops.date_confidence: inferred as to date. de.wikipedia notes the Wiesengrund firm's commercial tie to the Karplus and Herzberger works in Berlin, which is the documented Berlin thread; the fourteen-year courtship is implied by the 1937 marriage but no first meeting is dated in any source consulted. The 1923 date is the geographic dossier's, retained only to order the segment.
stops.campa: The Wiesengrund wine firm has commercial ties to the Karplus and Herzberger chemical works in Berlin, and in the Berlin years he comes to know Margarete Karplus, called Gretel, a chemist by training and a woman of exact judgment. No source dates their first meeting. The courtship will run fourteen years across three countries before it becomes a marriage. She will type the Dialectic of Enlightenment from his dictation, and after his death she will bring the Aesthetic Theory out of his typescripts into print.
suggested_refs: The Karplus und Herzberger works, Berlin

stops.name: Alsergrund, Vienna, the year of composition
stops.date_confidence: attested as to February 1925, the teachers, and the Schoenberg circle (en.wikipedia; de.wikipedia). The lodging is given as a pension in the ninth district; the exact address was not pinned, so the coordinate is district-level.
stops.campa: He takes a room in the ninth district and comes to Vienna to become a composer. Alban Berg accepts him as a pupil in composition; Eduard Steuermann teaches him piano; the circle around Arnold Schoenberg opens to him and never quite lets him in. What he carries away is not a career in music but a conviction he never afterward abandons: that the state of the material at a given moment is a historical fact, and that no composer can write behind it. He is twenty-one, and the twelve-tone method is not yet a decade old.
suggested_refs: The Schoenberg circle in Vienna, 1925-1926

stops.name: Hietzing, Trauttmansdorffgasse 27
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to venue. de.wikipedia, 'Alban Berg', confirms Adorno as Berg's composition pupil in 1925/26 but gives no address for the lessons. Trauttmansdorffgasse 27 is the widely reported Berg residence and is geocoded here exactly (Nominatim: 48.1830754, 16.2955342); the dossier's coordinate was 330 metres off and has been replaced. That the lessons were held at the house is not attested in a source reached this session.
stops.campa: The lessons are held at Berg's house in Hietzing, out past Schönbrunn, where the composer of Wozzeck works slowly and shows a pupil what slowness costs. Adorno calls him master and teacher for the rest of his life and writes about his music for forty years. That the lessons happened in the house is not attested; the address is Berg's, and the rest is inference. The Vienna year ends without a composing career. Berg dies in 1935, at fifty, and Adorno's book on him appears in 1968.
suggested_refs: Adorno, Alban Berg: Master of the Smallest Link (1968)

segments.name: The Habilitation and the Closing Doors

stops.name: Frankfurt, the Institute changes hands
stops.date_confidence: attested. felix_weil.journey.json dates Horkheimer's assumption of the chair to 1931 and names Adorno among the recruits; max_horkheimer.journey.json carries the same event. Adorno's own salaried membership of the Institute comes later, in the New York years. Month is an ordering convention.
stops.campa: Max Horkheimer takes the chair of social philosophy and the direction of the Institute for Social Research, the endowment Felix Weil built out of his father's grain fortune, and begins gathering the people the school will later be named for. Adorno is one of them, alongside Erich Fromm and Herbert Marcuse. He is not yet on the payroll and will not be for years; the relation at this stage is a friendship and a program. Horkheimer's inaugural address sets the terms: philosophy put to work on empirical social research.
suggested_refs: Horkheimer's 1931 inaugural address on the present situation of social philosophy
sources: felix_weil.journey.json, stop 'Frankfurt am Main, Horkheimer takes the chair'

stops.name: Frankfurt, the habilitation on Kierkegaard
stops.date_confidence: attested but frequently misdated. The Stanford Encyclopedia gives 1930 for the Kierkegaard Habilitationsschrift under Paul Tillich; en.wikipedia gives submission in mid-1929 and faculty approval in February 1931. The bare 1930 is wrong at both ends and is not used here. The inaugural lecture is dated 7 May 1931 by the geographic dossier; the Stanford Encyclopedia dates it only to 1931.
stops.campa: After a first attempt under Cornelius fails, he submits a study of Kierkegaard's aesthetics to the theologian Paul Tillich, who sponsors it; the faculty approves it in February 1931 and he becomes a Privatdozent. In May he gives the inaugural lecture, The Actuality of Philosophy, and tells the assembled faculty that philosophy can no longer deliver a totality, that it has to work like a lock-picker on the fragments the sciences leave lying about. The lecture is not printed in his lifetime.
suggested_refs: 'Die Aktualität der Philosophie', inaugural lecture, University of Frankfurt, 1931
sources: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

stops.name: Frankfurt, the book and the day it appears
stops.date_confidence: attested. en.wikipedia records that Kierkegaard: Construction of the Aesthetic was published on the day Hitler assumed dictatorial powers, which is the Enabling Act of 23 March 1933. The place of publication is Germany; the Frankfurt pin is the city of his working life rather than a documented printing house.
stops.campa: Kierkegaard: Construction of the Aesthetic, the habilitation revised for print, is published on the twenty-third of March 1933. On the same day the Reichstag passes the Enabling Act and hands Hitler the power to legislate without it. The book argues that Kierkegaard's inwardness is furnished like a nineteenth-century bourgeois apartment, that the interior is not an escape from society but its most private room. Almost nobody in Germany is reading philosophy criticism that week.
suggested_refs: Kierkegaard: Konstruktion des Ästhetischen (Tübingen, 1933)

stops.name: Institute for Social Research, the licence withdrawn
stops.date_confidence: attested for September 1933 (en.wikipedia): the teaching licence revoked under the racial legislation, and searches of the Institute and the family home. A further claim in the dossier, that he was barred from the Reich Chamber of Literature as non-Aryan at the same moment, is standardly dated 1934 or 1935 and could not be confirmed at all in the fetched text; it is not asserted here. Departure into exile in April 1934 per the Stanford Encyclopedia.
stops.campa: In September his venia legendi, the right to teach in a German university, is revoked under the new racial legislation. He is thirty, and the career takes a few minutes of paperwork to end. The Institute has already moved its endowment out of the country and most of its people with it; Horkheimer is gone, Marcuse is gone, the Frankfurt house will be seized. Adorno stays on in Germany for months longer than is prudent, half expecting the thing to pass, and does not leave until April 1934.
suggested_refs: The Institute's Frankfurt building, seized 1933
sources: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

segments.name: Oxford, Paris, and the Name Hektor Rottweiler

stops.name: Merton College, Oxford
stops.date_confidence: attested for June 1934 registration as an advanced student (en.wikipedia; Stanford Encyclopedia). The coordinate is the corpus pin for Merton College, inherited byte-identical from tolkien.journey.json rather than re-geocoded.
stops.campa: With help from the Academic Assistance Council he registers at Merton as an advanced student, a doctor of philosophy of thirty made a pupil again, supervised by Gilbert Ryle and working on a critique of Husserl that will take twenty years to become a book. He is neither welcome nor unwelcome; he is simply of no use to Oxford. He learns English properly and crosses the Channel whenever the money allows. For these years he calls himself an intellectual in emigration.
stops.quote: Ethics today means not being at home in one's house.
stops.quote_source: Minima Moralia, Part One, 'Asylum for the homeless' (1951), written out of these exile years
suggested_refs: The Academic Assistance Council files on refugee scholars, 1933-1936
sources: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

stops.name: Paris, the letter of the second of August
stops.date_confidence: attested. The letter of 2 August 1935 is printed in New Left Review I/81, 'Theodor Adorno: Letters to Walter Benjamin'; the repeated Oxford-to-Paris trips to see Gretel, Benjamin and Horkheimer are given by en.wikipedia. Paris coordinate inherited from the corpus canonical pin used in max_horkheimer.journey.json.
stops.campa: He comes over from Oxford to see Gretel, Horkheimer and Benjamin, and on the second of August writes Benjamin the long letter about the arcades project: praise first, then pages of objection to the notion of a collective dream-image, then a demand that the dialectic be driven all the way down. The friendship runs through such letters for the rest of Benjamin's life, and this one survives in print in New Left Review's collection of the letters to Benjamin. Adorno is thirty-one. Benjamin is forty-three.
stops.quote: the liberation of things from the curse of being useful
stops.quote_source: Adorno, letter to Walter Benjamin, 2 August 1935, New Left Review I/81
suggested_refs: The Adorno-Benjamin letters on the Passagenwerk, 1935-1938
sources: New Left Review I/81, 'Theodor Adorno: Letters to Walter Benjamin'

stops.name: Oxford, the name Hektor Rottweiler
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the pseudonym, the essay, and the journal (Zeitschrift für Sozialforschung, 1936), corroborated against the en.wikipedia publication history. The place is not: he was writing from Oxford and still travelling into Germany, and the journal was produced in exile, so the Oxford pin is where the author sat rather than where the essay was printed. Month arbitrary.
stops.campa: The essay On Jazz appears in the Institute's journal signed Hektor Rottweiler, a name assembled out of a Homeric hero and a guard dog. The essay is contemptuous of jazz in a way that has embarrassed his readers ever since; it hears in the syncopation not liberty but a deviation the industry has standardized and priced. He is still travelling into Germany on family business, and a Jewish signature on that argument would be dangerous in a customs shed.
suggested_refs: 'Über Jazz', Zeitschrift für Sozialforschung, 1936, signed Hektor Rottweiler

stops.name: Paddington, the registry office
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date (en.wikipedia; de.wikipedia gives the London district). The specific registry building was not identified in any source reached, so the coordinate is district-level for Paddington.
stops.campa: On the eighth of September, in the Paddington district register office, Theodor Wiesengrund Adorno and Margarete Karplus are married. He is thirty-three, she is thirty-five, and the courtship has run fourteen years, most of them conducted by post between cities neither of them could stay in. There is no wedding of the kind the two families would have staged in Frankfurt ten years earlier. They will be married thirty-two years and have no children.
suggested_refs: Paddington district register office, marriage of 8 September 1937

stops.name: Paris, the last meeting with Benjamin
stops.date_confidence: attested by max_horkheimer.journey.json, which dates Horkheimer's brief European return and the Paris meeting to October 1937 and records that Horkheimer and Adorno sent Benjamin's manuscripts back with demands for revision. The Baudelaire dispute proper runs into 1938. Day is an ordering convention.
stops.campa: Horkheimer crosses back to Europe in October and the three of them meet in Paris; it is the last time Horkheimer sees Benjamin. Benjamin is living on an Institute stipend and sending the Baudelaire essays to New York, where Adorno reads them and returns them with demands for revision. Benjamin accepts the demands and resents them. Adorno will spend twenty-nine years editing him. In 1940 Benjamin dies at Portbou on the Spanish border, the Gestapo behind him.
suggested_refs: Benjamin's Baudelaire essays and the 1938 exchange with Adorno
sources: max_horkheimer.journey.json, stop 'Paris, the last meeting with Benjamin'
New Left Review I/81, 'Theodor Adorno: Letters to Walter Benjamin'

stops.name: Columbia University, Morningside Heights
stops.date_confidence: attested. Sailing and arrival 16 February 1938 (en.wikipedia); the Christopher Street address from de.wikipedia; the Institute's Columbia building at 429 West 117th Street from max_horkheimer.journey.json, herbert_marcuse.journey.json and felix_weil.journey.json, which together attest the 1934 crossing. Fromm's 1939 departure amid financial retrenchment is from max_horkheimer.journey.json. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the three existing files.
stops.campa: He and Gretel dock in New York on the sixteenth of February and take a flat on Christopher Street in the Village. The Institute has been housed since 1934 in a Columbia building on West 117th Street, and the people are all here: Horkheimer, Friedrich Pollock, Leo Löwenthal, Herbert Marcuse, Erich Fromm. He is thirty-four and has no German position to go back to. Adorno becomes a formal member and, fast, Horkheimer's closest collaborator. Fromm leaves the following year as the Institute's money tightens.
suggested_refs: 429 West 117th Street, New York, the Institute's American house

stops.name: Newark, the Princeton Radio Research Project
stops.date_confidence: attested for the appointment, Lazarsfeld's role, and the 1941 loss of funding (en.wikipedia). The office address in Newark was not located; the coordinate is city-level. Month is an ordering convention.
stops.campa: Paul Lazarsfeld hires him to run the music division of a Rockefeller-funded study of what radio does to listeners, and installs him in an office in Newark. Lazarsfeld wants measurement; Adorno wants to know what the measuring instrument itself has already assumed. He argues that a research design asking listeners to rate what they like has conceded in advance that liking is the point. Each man will later publish his own account of the failure. The Rockefeller Foundation declines to renew the music division in 1941.
stops.quote: Under monopoly all mass culture is identical, and the lines of its artificial framework begin to show through.
stops.quote_source: Adorno and Horkheimer, 'The Culture Industry: Enlightenment as Mass Deception', written later in California
suggested_refs: Adorno, 'Scientific Experiences of a European Scholar in America' (1968)

stops.name: Pacific Palisades, the move west and the dictation
stops.date_confidence: attested for November 1941 and for the émigré colony (en.wikipedia). The dossier's street address, 316 South Kenter Avenue, geocodes to Brentwood rather than Pacific Palisades and is supported by neither cited source, so it is not used; the coordinate is the corpus canonical Pacific Palisades pin from max_horkheimer.journey.json. The mimeographed Philosophische Fragmente is dated May 1944 by en.wikipedia; Gretel Adorno's typing and note-keeping from max_horkheimer.journey.json.
stops.campa: In November he and Gretel follow Horkheimer to the Pacific coast, into the émigré colony strung along the canyons above Santa Monica bay: Thomas Mann on San Remo Drive, Brecht, Hanns Eisler, Schoenberg over in Brentwood. Here he and Horkheimer begin dictating to each other, and to Gretel, who types and keeps the notes, the book they are calling Philosophische Fragmente. The dictation runs on for the better part of three years. A mimeographed edition of a few hundred copies goes out in May 1944.
stops.quote: Films, radio and magazines make up a system which is uniform as a whole and in every part.
stops.quote_source: Adorno and Horkheimer, 'The Culture Industry: Enlightenment as Mass Deception', 1944
suggested_refs: Philosophische Fragmente, mimeographed edition, Los Angeles, May 1944
sources: max_horkheimer.journey.json, stop 'Pacific Palisades, the Philosophische Fragmente'
marxists.org, 'The Culture Industry: Enlightenment as Mass Deception'

stops.name: Los Angeles, citizenship and two collaborations
stops.date_confidence: attested. Naturalisation November 1943 (de.wikipedia); the advice to Thomas Mann on the music of Doktor Faustus and the Rockefeller-funded film-music work with Hanns Eisler (en.wikipedia). Composing for the Films is published in 1947 under Eisler's name alone, Adorno having withdrawn his; that detail is not asserted in the campa because it was not re-verified this session.
stops.campa: He is naturalized as a United States citizen in November 1943, in the middle of a war against the country that expelled him. Thomas Mann, two streets away, is writing a novel about a composer who buys genius from the devil, and consults Adorno on the music; the twelve-tone technique in Doktor Faustus comes out of these conversations and out of the Vienna year. With Hanns Eisler he is at work on a book about how a film score makes an image feel inevitable. It appears in 1947 as Composing for the Films.
stops.quote: Amusement under late capitalism is the prolongation of work. It is sought after as an escape from the mechanised work process.
stops.quote_source: Adorno and Horkheimer, 'The Culture Industry: Enlightenment as Mass Deception', 1944
suggested_refs: Thomas Mann, Die Entstehung des Doktor Faustus, on Adorno's musical advice

stops.name: Berkeley, the F-scale
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the collaboration and the American Jewish Committee funding under Horkheimer's scientific direction (max_horkheimer.journey.json; en.wikipedia, which lists Berkeley among Adorno's institutions). Personal residence or travel to Berkeley is not established in any source consulted and remains reconstruction. The coordinate is Sather Tower, the campus centre; the dossier's point fell 1.6 kilometres east in Strawberry Canyon and has been replaced. Month arbitrary.
stops.campa: The American Jewish Committee funds a program of research on antisemitism under Horkheimer's scientific direction, and its largest study puts Adorno with a team of Berkeley psychologists: Else Frenkel-Brunswik, Daniel Levinson, Nevitt Sanford. They build a scale of items meant to measure not opinions but the personality structure underneath them, and call it the F-scale, F for fascist. The instrument is Freudian in its depth and American in its method. The Authoritarian Personality appears in 1950.
suggested_refs: The Authoritarian Personality (New York, 1950), Studies in Prejudice series
sources: max_horkheimer.journey.json, stop 'New York, the American Jewish Committee'

stops.name: Amsterdam, the Querido imprint
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 1947 Querido edition (en.wikipedia). Month unknown, defaulted. The English translation by John Cumming, Herder and Herder, New York, 1972, is confirmed by en.wikipedia, 'Dialectic of Enlightenment'; Edmund Jephcott's retranslation from the corrected German text appears from Stanford in 2002.
stops.campa: The book dictated in a California canyon is published in Amsterdam by Querido, the house that has been printing exiled German literature since 1933. It is now called Dialectic of Enlightenment, and it argues that reason, in freeing itself from myth, became a myth of its own, and that the culture industry supplies the reconciliation society itself refuses. It sells almost nothing. John Cumming's English translation appears from Herder and Herder in 1972, twenty-five years later.
stops.quote: The culture industry perpetually cheats its consumers of what it perpetually promises. The promissory note which, with its plots and staging, it draws on pleasure is endlessly prolonged.
stops.quote_source: Adorno and Horkheimer, 'The Culture Industry: Enlightenment as Mass Deception', Dialectic of Enlightenment
suggested_refs: Querido Verlag, Amsterdam, exile imprint 1933-1950
sources: marxists.org, 'The Culture Industry: Enlightenment as Mass Deception'

stops.name: University of Frankfurt, the return
stops.date_confidence: contested, left unresolved. The Stanford Encyclopedia says he returned to Frankfurt in 1949 to posts in philosophy and sociology; en.wikipedia says he left America at the end of October 1949 and gives 1950 as the return to Frankfurt. Departure from the United States in October 1949 is common to both; whether the teaching resumes in the 1949/50 winter semester or later is not settled here. Permanent resettlement dated August 1953 by the geographic dossier.
stops.campa: He leaves the United States at the end of October and comes back to a bombed city and a university that offers him Horkheimer's chair to hold as a deputy. He is forty-six and has been out of Germany for fifteen years. The lecture halls fill; the students are young men back from the Wehrmacht and from prisoner-of-war camps, and he stands in front of them speaking a German he kept intact by using it in California. Whether he teaches the winter semester of 1949 or waits for 1950, the sources do not agree.
suggested_refs: The rebuilt University of Frankfurt, Bockenheim campus, 1949
sources: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

stops.name: Frankfurt, Minima Moralia
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1951 publication (en.wikipedia); month unknown, defaulted. The English edition is 1974, translated by Edmund Jephcott for New Left Books, per en.wikipedia's Adorno bibliography, and not Verso 1978 as the dossier had it; Verso is the later corporate identity and carries the reprints.
stops.campa: The aphorisms written in exile and dedicated to Horkheimer are published in Frankfurt: fragments on damaged life, on gift-giving, on the shape of doors, on the impossibility of a private sphere that is not already administered. The eighteenth, Asylum for the Homeless, works through what it means to own furniture in a century of displaced persons, and closes on a sentence about right life and wrong. Edmund Jephcott's English version comes out from New Left Books in 1974, twenty-three years after the German.
stops.quote: There is no right life in the wrong one.
stops.quote_source: Minima Moralia, Part One, aphorism 18, 'Asylum for the homeless' (1951)
suggested_refs: Minima Moralia: Reflexionen aus dem beschädigten Leben (Frankfurt, 1951)

stops.name: Schloss Kranichstein, Darmstadt
stops.date_confidence: attested for the span 1951-1958 at the Darmstadt International Summer Courses for New Music (en.wikipedia). The month is an ordering convention for a summer course. The Mahler book is dated 1960 by en.wikipedia.
stops.campa: Every summer through 1958 he teaches at the International Summer Courses for New Music, in the hunting lodge outside Darmstadt where the postwar avant-garde assembles. He defends the new music against the restoration, then turns on the young serialists, Boulez, Stockhausen, Nono, and tells them a totally determined row is a piece of administration and not a piece of freedom. In 1960 he publishes Mahler: A Musical Physiognomy, on the composer who let the broken material stay audible.
suggested_refs: The Internationale Ferienkurse für Neue Musik, Darmstadt, 1951-1958

stops.name: Senckenberganlage, the Institute reopens
stops.date_confidence: attested. The date 14 November 1951, the McCloy High Commission funding and Weil's money are from max_horkheimer.journey.json; felix_weil.journey.json for the same date names Adorno and Pollock as having returned to West Germany while Marcuse, Löwenthal and Kirchheimer stayed. Coordinate is the corpus canonical Institute pin, inherited byte-identical; Nominatim puts the building at 50.1184258, 8.6538963, some seventy metres away.
stops.campa: On the fourteenth of November the Institute for Social Research opens a new building on the Senckenberganlage, paid for in part out of John J. McCloy's High Commission fund and in part by Felix Weil, who financed the first one thirty years earlier. Adorno and Pollock have come back to West Germany; Marcuse, Löwenthal and Kirchheimer have stayed in America. The Institute's first large study, the Gruppenexperiment, records what Germans say about the recent past when they believe they are talking among themselves.
suggested_refs: Gruppenexperiment: ein Studienbericht (Frankfurt, 1955)
sources: max_horkheimer.journey.json, stop 'Frankfurt am Main, the new house on the Senckenberganlage'
felix_weil.journey.json, stop 'Frankfurt am Main, the institute reopens'

stops.name: Beverly Hills, the Hacker Foundation
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 1952 research directorship at the Hacker Psychiatric Foundation in Beverly Hills (Stanford Encyclopedia). Month unknown, defaulted. The astrology study, The Stars Down to Earth, is dated to this stay by the standard literature but was not re-verified against a fetched source this session; the citizenship-preservation motive is likewise widely reported and not re-verified. Coordinate is city-level for Beverly Hills.
stops.campa: He goes back to California for the better part of a year as research director of Friedrich Hacker's psychiatric foundation in Beverly Hills. He spends the months analysing the astrology column of the Los Angeles Times, item by item, and writes The Stars Down to Earth: the horoscope as a form that flatters the reader's autonomy while telling him exactly what to do, addressed to people who half believe it and know that they half believe it. Then he goes home to Frankfurt for good.
suggested_refs: Adorno, 'The Stars Down to Earth: The Los Angeles Times Astrology Column' (1952-53)
sources: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Theodor W. Adorno'

stops.name: Frankfurt, the direction handed over
stops.date_confidence: contested, and the contradiction is carried rather than resolved. en.wikipedia dates Adorno's directorship of the Institute to 1958; max_horkheimer.journey.json records the handover of day-to-day direction over several preceding years and states plainly that the sources do not agree whether it happened in 1958 or in stages toward Horkheimer's 1959 retirement. Election as chairman of the German Sociological Society is dated 1963 by en.wikipedia. Month arbitrary.
stops.campa: Horkheimer gives up the day-to-day direction of the Institute and Adorno takes it, at fifty-five, with the chair in philosophy and sociology to go with it. Whether the transfer happens in 1958 or by stages into 1959, the record does not settle. He is by now the most audible intellectual in the Federal Republic, and what he argues in public is what the German past requires of Germans who were not there. His lectures and talks go out at night on Hessischer Rundfunk.
suggested_refs: Adorno's Hessischer Rundfunk broadcasts, 1950s-1960s
sources: max_horkheimer.journey.json, stop 'Frankfurt am Main, the chair given up'

segments.name: The Public Voice and the Students

stops.name: Frankfurt, The Jargon of Authenticity
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1964 publication and for the book's target, Heideggerian language (en.wikipedia). Month unknown, defaulted. That the text began as a chapter of Negative Dialectics is standard in the literature and is stated here as such rather than as a fetched citation.
stops.campa: He publishes a hundred and fifty pages against a vocabulary: encounter, concern, commission, the authentic, the primordial, words that Martin Heidegger and his imitators use to give ordinary German the tone of the sacred. Adorno's charge is not that the philosophy behind them is wrong but that the diction does the arguing, conferring an aura on whatever it touches and exempting it from examination. He means the piece as a chapter of the book on dialectics; it grows until it has to stand alone.
suggested_refs: Jargon der Eigentlichkeit: Zur deutschen Ideologie (Frankfurt, 1964)

stops.name: Frankfurt, Negative Dialectics
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1966 for both Negative Dialektik and 'Erziehung nach Auschwitz' (en.wikipedia). Months unknown, defaulted. E. B. Ashton's English translation is Seabury Press, 1973, per en.wikipedia's Adorno bibliography; the Routledge edition is a later reprint of the same translation.
stops.campa: Negative Dialectics appears: a philosophy that refuses the moment where the negation turns positive and the system closes. Thinking is to stay with the non-identical, with whatever the concept fails to catch, and it is not to console. The same year he publishes Education after Auschwitz and states the demand without any argument around it, that the first requirement of all education is that Auschwitz not happen again, that this precedes every justification, and that it has not been met.
suggested_refs: Negative Dialektik (1966), trans. E. B. Ashton, Seabury Press, 1973

stops.name: University of Vienna, the new right-wing radicalism
stops.date_confidence: attested for the lecture, the date, the city, and the 2019 publication (en.wikipedia). The specific lecture hall was not confirmed, so the coordinate is the university rather than a room. The English edition's translator and publisher could not be verified this session: the Polity Books page returned empty and a New York Review of Books article returned 404.
stops.campa: Invited by Austrian socialist students, he speaks in Vienna on the aspects of the new right-wing radicalism, at a moment when the NPD is entering West German state parliaments. He tells the hall that the social conditions which produced fascism have not gone anywhere, that the movement now uses democratic forms against democracy, and that in this kind of politics the propaganda technique is the substance. A tape survives in a drawer. It is transcribed and published in 2019.
suggested_refs: Aspekte des neuen Rechtsradikalismus, Vienna lecture of 6 April 1967, published 2019

stops.name: Frankfurt, the sociology congress
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the address and its text, given by marxists.org as the 1968 Frankfurt Sociology Congress address, 'Late Capitalism or Industrial Society?'. The chairmanship of the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Soziologie from 1963 is from en.wikipedia. The exact congress days were not re-verified this session; the month is taken from the standard dating of the sixteenth Deutscher Soziologentag.
stops.campa: As chairman of the German Sociological Society, elected in 1963, he opens the sixteenth Deutscher Soziologentag with a question put as a title: late capitalism or industrial society? His answer is that the two terms are not interchangeable labels but rival accounts of what runs the world, and that Karl Marx's categories were not superseded by the failure of the proletariat to do what Marx expected of it. The congress meets in Frankfurt in April 1968.
stops.quote: The power of the relations of production, which were not overthrown, is greater than ever, and yet at the same time they are, as objectively anachronistic, everywhere diseased, damaged, riddled with holes.
stops.quote_source: Adorno, 'Late Capitalism or Industrial Society?', 1968 Frankfurt Sociology Congress
suggested_refs: Verhandlungen des 16. Deutschen Soziologentages, Frankfurt 1968

stops.name: Institute for Social Research, the police called
stops.date_confidence: attested. de.wikipedia records the forced entry of 31 January 1969, the decision by Adorno and Ludwig von Friedeburg as directors to call the police and report the occupiers, and the inner conflict this cost a man who had spent his life opposing policing and surveillance. The figure of seventy-six arrested and Marcuse's public objection are from en.wikipedia and max_horkheimer.journey.json.
stops.campa: On the thirty-first of January students force their way into the Institute and demand a discussion of the political situation. Adorno and Ludwig von Friedeburg, as directors, telephone the police and give evidence against the occupiers; seventy-six are arrested. He has spent his working life writing about surveillance, the administered world, and what a state does to those whose names it holds, and he has just used that apparatus on his own students. Marcuse, from California, tells him publicly that he was wrong.
suggested_refs: The Adorno-Marcuse correspondence on the German student movement, 1969

stops.name: University of Frankfurt, the twenty-second of April
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by de.wikipedia, 'Busenattentat', which also corrects the lecture title to 'Einführung in dialektisches Denken' and supplies the chalked demands, the five minutes he asked for, the rose and tulip petals, and the briefcase held over his head. Only Hannah Weitemeier is publicly named of the three. The quote is a secondary re-quotation: New Left Review I/233 cites an Adorno caption in Stern; no facsimile of Stern was seen.
stops.campa: He arrives to lecture on the introduction to dialectical thinking and finds demands chalked on the blackboard: that he account for the police. He asks the hall for five minutes to decide whether to go on. Three women then come up onto the podium, bare their breasts and try to scatter rose and tulip petals over him. He gathers his papers, holds his briefcase above his head, and leaves the room. Of the three, only Hannah Weitemeier is ever publicly named.
stops.quote: I proposed a theoretical model for thought. How could I suspect that people would want to realize it with Molotov-cocktails?
stops.quote_source: Adorno, caption in Stern, 1969, as reproduced in Esther Leslie, New Left Review I/233
suggested_refs: de.wikipedia, 'Busenattentat', 22 April 1969
sources: New Left Review I/233, Esther Leslie, 'Introduction to Adorno-Marcuse Correspondence'

stops.name: Frankfurt, the letter to Marcuse
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The letter of 5 May 1969 is printed in the Adorno-Marcuse correspondence on the German student movement, field-journal.com editorial edition. Marcuse's location in San Diego at this date is standard and was not re-verified this session.
stops.campa: He writes to Herbert Marcuse in California, in an argument conducted by post all spring about what a theorist owes a movement that claims him. Marcuse holds that the students are the practice the theory demanded; Adorno holds that a theory which lets itself be used as a slogan has stopped being a theory. They have known each other since Horkheimer gathered them both into the Institute in 1931, and neither writes as though the friendship were in danger. Neither persuades the other.
stops.quote: I think that you are deluding yourself in being unable to go on without participating in the student stunts
stops.quote_source: Adorno, letter to Herbert Marcuse, 5 May 1969
suggested_refs: Adorno and Marcuse, Correspondence on the German Student Movement, 1969
sources: field-journal.com, 'Theodor Adorno and Herbert Marcuse: Correspondence on the German Student Movement'

stops.name: Frankfurt, the last manuscript and the witness box
stops.date_confidence: attested. Stichworte completed June 1969 (en.wikipedia); the letter of 19 June 1969 to Marcuse from the field-journal edition; the trial date from de.wikipedia, 'Hans-Jürgen Krahl', verbatim: 'In dem folgenden Prozess gegen Krahl am 18. Juli 1969 war Adorno als Zeuge geladen.' Note the framing: he was summoned as a witness in a breach-of-the-peace prosecution, which is weaker than the dossier's 'testified against'.
stops.campa: In June he finishes Stichworte, the last book he sees through the press, and writes to Marcuse that he is in a phase of extreme depression whose cause is in no way psychological. On the eighteenth of July he is summoned as a witness in the prosecution of Hans-Jürgen Krahl, his own doctoral student and the leader of the January occupation, on a charge of breach of the peace arising from the forced entry of the thirty-first of January. He gives his evidence.
stops.quote: I find myself in a phase of extreme depression, whose cause is in no way psychological
stops.quote_source: Adorno, letter to Herbert Marcuse, 19 June 1969
suggested_refs: Stichworte: Kritische Modelle 2 (Frankfurt, 1969)

stops.name: Zermatt, the cable car to Trockener Steg
stops.date_confidence: attested with two corrections to the dossier. de.wikipedia states 'Ungenügend akklimatisiert, fuhr er mit einer Seilbahn auf fast 3000 m.ü.M. und wanderte dann zur Gandegghütte (3030 m.ü.M.)': he rode the cable car and only then walked. The dossier's 'hiked to nearly 3,000 metres' and 'against medical advice' are both unsupported and are not written here. The exact day of the ascent is not recorded; 2 August orders the segment inside the attested early-August window. The Gandegghütte geocodes to 45.9641, 7.7256.
stops.campa: He and Gretel take the Valais holiday of a couple who have holidayed in the Alps for years. Insufficiently acclimatised, he rides the cable car up to Trockener Steg, near three thousand metres, and walks from there to the Gandegghütte, which stands at three thousand and thirty. It is a short walk on a good path. Nothing in the record mentions a doctor's warning, given or ignored, and nothing mentions a climb up from the valley on foot. His heart begins to trouble him on the mountain.
suggested_refs: The Gandegghütte above Zermatt, 3,030 m

stops.name: Visp, the Krankenhaus St. Maria
stops.date_confidence: attested. de.wikipedia, verbatim: 'Als er Herzbeschwerden bekam, wurde er ins Visper Krankenhaus St. Maria gebracht. Dort erlag er am Morgen des 6. Augusts 1969 einem Herzinfarkt.' The hospital name, the town, the morning, and the cause are all in the source. Gretel's death notice wording is from the geographic dossier and was not re-verified against a printed notice.
stops.campa: He is brought down the valley to the Krankenhaus St. Maria in Visp, and dies there of a heart attack on the morning of the sixth of August. He is sixty-five, and he has been in Switzerland a matter of days. Gretel's notice says he died quietly in his sleep. Later retellings make the April lecture hall the cause of the August heart attack, and the story has been repeated for the rest of the century. Four months separate the two events, and no physician's word connects them.
suggested_refs: Krankenhaus St. Maria, Visp, Canton of Valais

stops.name: Frankfurter Hauptfriedhof, the grave
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the cemetery, dated only to August 1969 by the sources; the exact day of burial is a gap and 7 August is an ordering date placed after the death rather than defaulted to the first of the month, which would invert the sequence. de.wikipedia: 'Adornos Grab befindet sich auf dem Frankfurter Hauptfriedhof.' The grave field and section number were not found. Coordinate corrected to 50.1361, 8.6849 per de.wikipedia's cemetery article; the dossier's geographic entry was 580 metres off and disagreed with its own afterlife entry.
stops.campa: He is buried in the main cemetery of Frankfurt, in the city he was born in, left in 1934, and came back to in 1949 when few of the exiles came back at all. Arthur Schopenhauer lies in the same ground, dead a hundred and nine years. Gretel Adorno survives him by twenty-four years and spends much of that time on his papers. Aesthetic Theory is on the desk in Frankfurt, unfinished. The day of the burial is nowhere in the record, which gives the month and no more, and the grave's field and section go unrecorded as well.
suggested_refs: Frankfurter Hauptfriedhof, which also holds Schopenhauer's grave

stops.name: Frankfurt, Aesthetic Theory
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1970 posthumous publication (en.wikipedia); month unknown, defaulted. Gretel Adorno and Rolf Tiedemann as the editors who constructed the text from the last typescripts is from the geographic dossier's account and is standard in the literature; the editorial history was not re-verified line by line this session.
stops.campa: Gretel Adorno and Rolf Tiedemann assemble the book out of the last typescripts and publish it in 1970. It has no first sentence in the ordinary sense and no chapter that comes before another by right; Adorno has planned it so that a reader can enter anywhere, on the ground that a philosophy of art which built a staircase would have betrayed its object on the first step. What it says is that art is autonomous and a social fact at once, and that neither half can be let go.
suggested_refs: Ästhetische Theorie, ed. Gretel Adorno and Rolf Tiedemann (Frankfurt, 1970)

stops.name: Frankfurt, the prize
stops.date_confidence: attested. de.wikipedia, 'Theodor-W.-Adorno-Preis': awarded by the city of Frankfurt every three years since 1977, for philosophy, music, theatre or film, presented by the mayor, carrying 50,000 euros, and given after only two years in 2003 to mark the centenary. Named winners include Habermas 1980, Boulez 1992, Godard 1995, Derrida 2001, von Trotta 2018. Month unknown, defaulted.
stops.campa: The city of Frankfurt establishes the Theodor W. Adorno Prize, awarded every three years for work in philosophy, music, theatre or film and handed over by the mayor. Jürgen Habermas, who was his assistant at the Institute, takes it in 1980; Pierre Boulez, whom he told at Darmstadt that total serialism was administration, takes it in 1992; Jean-Luc Godard in 1995. In 2003 the city breaks its own three-year interval and awards it after two, for the centenary of his birth.
suggested_refs: Jacques Derrida's 2001 Adorno Prize lecture, 'Fichus', delivered in Frankfurt

stops.name: Senckenberganlage, the traffic light
stops.date_confidence: attested. de.wikipedia, verbatim: 'Adorno hatte sich seit 1962 für den Bau einer Ampel an der vielbefahrenen Straße zwischen dem Institut und dem Universitätscampus in Frankfurt-Bockenheim eingesetzt; allerdings wurde die Ampel erst 1987 installiert.' Month unknown, defaulted. The dossier's coordinate lay 1.1 km northeast of the street; this one is placed on the Senckenberganlage beside the Institute, Nominatim giving the street at 50.1157, 8.6518 with a narrow longitude box.
stops.campa: From 1962 Adorno petitions the city of Frankfurt for a pedestrian signal on the Senckenberganlage, the wide and heavily trafficked road between the Institute and the Bockenheim campus, which his staff and his students cross several times a day and which he crosses himself to get to work. The city does not build it. The light goes up in 1987, eighteen years after his death and twenty-five years after the first request. Frankfurt calls it the Adorno-Ampel.
suggested_refs: The Adorno-Ampel, Senckenberganlage, Frankfurt-Bockenheim

stops.name: Bockenheim, the glass cube
stops.date_confidence: attested in detail by de.wikipedia, 'Adorno-Denkmal': Vadim Zakharov, five glass panes of 350 kg each with 2.50 m edges, parquet floor, desk, chair, dusk-triggered lamp, Mälzel metronome on a copy of Negative Dialektik (1966), Minima Moralia and Aesthetic Theory quotations set in white marble and black granite paving laid as a labyrinth, about 220,000 euros from the city budget, inaugurated 10 October 2003. The Bockenheim square, renamed Tilly-Edinger-Platz after the removal, geocodes to 50.1166573, 8.6487880; the dossier's point was some 700 metres off. Relocation to the Westend campus in April 2016, coordinate there 50.1284, 8.6656.
stops.campa: For the centenary the city commissions the Russian artist Vadim Zakharov to build a monument, and he builds Adorno's study: five panes of glass at three hundred and fifty kilos each, enclosing a parquet floor, a desk, a chair, a lamp that comes on at dusk, and a Mälzel metronome resting on a copy of Negative Dialektik. Sentences from Minima Moralia and Aesthetic Theory are set into the paving around it in white marble and black granite, laid out as a labyrinth. The glass is broken again and again. In 2016 the whole thing is moved to the Westend campus, and the vandalism stops.
suggested_refs: Vadim Zakharov's Adorno-Denkmal, Frankfurt, 2003; relocated to Theodor-W.-Adorno-Platz, Campus Westend, April 2016
